newsitem.title: GREECE: Hopes dim for 20 missing in capsized Greek ship.
newsitem.headline: Hopes dim for 20 missing in capsized Greek ship.

text.p: Hopes were dimming on Sunday that navy, coast guard and private rescue vessels would locate 20 people missing in the Aegean Sea after a cargo ship capsized in bad weather.
"Divers who climbed on the ship's keel knocked but got no response," Merchant Marine Minister Stavros Soumakis told a news conference. "Let's hope that there is a chance there are survivors."

The cargo ship Distos capsized at about 2000 GMT on Saturday off the port of Kimi on the island of Evia. It had a crew of 18; one seaman was travelling with his wife while another with his wife and 10-year-old daughter.
The only crew member who has been rescued, nautical college student Christos Anagnostou, 18, told the coast guard two large waves engulfed the ship, which was carrying cement.
Anagnostou jumped into the sea after the Distos started listing and shot flares in the air, helping the coastguard spot the capsized ship, Soumakis said.
Merchant marine ministry sources said chances were very slim anyone could survive on the air trapped inside the ship, whose red keel was floating above the water.

"Passing ships, coastguard vessels, fishing boats and air force helicopters are searching the area for the 20 missing people, to this moment without success," the merchant marine ministry said in a statement.
The vessel, owned by the Heracles Cement company, was carrying 5,300 tonnes of cement from the central port town of Volos to the port of Piraeus, near Athens.
Many passenger vessels were advised to cancel their trips on Saturday due to storms in the Aegean Sea.

"When we notified the owning company that we had a signal their ship was in trouble, they did not know it was at sea and told us it was docked at the island of Skiathos overnight to avoid bad weather," Soumakis said.
He said the ship left the island of Skiathos in strong gale force winds, measuring about 9 knots.
"We did not give the ship an order to leave port. There was no need to transport the cargo during the holidays," Heracles Cement representative Nikos Mavros told a news conference.
Soumakis said his ministry was considering pulling the ship towards shallow waters near the coast of Evia.
"It is a very large operation and it must be studied carefully," he said.
